headline: Africa: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Africa: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
- Persian Gulf Region: US base in Bahrain remains low-staffed months after Iranian drone, missile strikes - report.
- Western Russia: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: RELIEF LAWSUIT - Pastor challenges NIDS requirement for hurricane aid.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 20 hours ago: RELIEF LAWSUIT - Pastor challenges NIDS requirement for hurricane aid.
Pastor Jeffrey Shuttleworth has filed a judicial review application in the Supreme Court challenging the Government’s decision requiring Jamaicans to register under the National Identification System (NIDS) to access Hurricane Melissa relief assistance. The senior pastor of Freedom Come Ministries International wants the Supreme Court to declare the decision illegal, null and void, and quash the requirement through an order of certiorari, as well as award costs.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 20 hours ago: Constitutional red flag raised over power to sell property for unpaid fees.
Solicitor General Marlene Aldred on Thursday raised a red flag in relation to Section 35(1) of the Registration (Shared Community) Act 2026, arguing that it is not consistent with Section 15 of the Constitution. Her pronouncement followed committee member Cleveland Tomlinson’s identification of an inconsistency in the bill, which he said warranted careful review.
United States: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

South America - bottom line: Dismantling of policies against violence leaves women with fewer tools to escape.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 9 hours ago: Dismantling of policies against violence leaves women with fewer tools to escape.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.
- The Moscow Times, 15 hours ago: Drone Strikes Kill 2 in Kursk and Bryansk Regions Amid Overnight Attacks.
In St. Petersburg, falling drone debris reportedly wounded a 44-year-old woman after damaging an apartment building.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 14 hours ago: "They were trying to build their lives": IT couple killed in Russian drone attack on Kharkiv.
A Russian Shahed drone hit a 15th-floor flat in Kharkiv on 26 November, killing 38-year-old IT specialists Daria and Valerii along with their cat.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Russians attack civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast: one killed, 12 injured.
One person was killed and 12 were injured in a Russian strike on a civilian business in Zhytomyr Oblast's Malyn hromada on the afternoon of 27 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 13 hours ago: Russian forces attack Lozova with jet-powered drones, injuring two people.
Russian forces struck Lozova in Kharkiv Oblast with jet-powered drones on 27 November, injuring two people and sparking fires at a house and warehouse.
Southern Europe - bottom line: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: We’d be ‘stupid’ not to: Poland defends $300M military AI deal with Palantir.
Poland's defense minister said it would be “wrong” not to use the software, despite concerns over reliance on American technology.
- Politico Europe, 18 hours ago: ‘Islam is Sharia’: Germany’s far-right leader attacks Le Pen on Muslims and Europe.
AfD’s Alice Weidel talks mass deportations, the right to Israel’s existence and peace with Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 19 hours ago: Democracy Digest: V4 Remain Critical of Budget as EU Summit Ends Without Deal.
Elsewhere, Ukrainian youth in hospital after setting himself on fire opposite Warsaw’s presidential palace; postal voting scrapped for Slovakia’s 2027 election; EU Parliament warns against Czechia’s public media reforms.
- Politico Europe, 23 hours ago: Bank of England boss warns AI must benefit humans.
Tech needs boundaries — "a bit like rearing children," says Andrew Bailey.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
- Africanews, 18 hours ago: Algeria condemns 'spillover' of Ukraine war into Libya.
Algeria on Thursday condemned what it called the ‘spillover’ of the war in Ukraine into Libya, after Kyiv’s attack on two Russian vessels off eastern Libya. Two Libyan soldiers were killed in Sunday’s drone strikes which sank a Russian warship and targeted a cargo ship in Libyan waters.
- Africanews, 18 hours ago: Italy says not informed about Ukraine drone strike on Russian ships in Libya.
Italy has joined the voices expressing concern about Ukraine’s attack on Russia ships in Libyan waters. Rome was not informed of Sunday’s drone strike, the country’s foreign minister told parliament on Thursday, warning that further military action could jeopardise efforts to reunify Libya.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 22 hours ago: Sudan: UN Condemns Drone Strikes That Killed 17 Civilians in Blue Nile.
[Dabanga] The United Nations has condemned drone strikes in Blue Nile that reportedly killed 17 civilians in Ed Damazin, as fighting escalates, and displacement deepens across the region. UN Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Wednesday that the UN remained "deeply concerned by the escalation of hostilities in Blue Nile state", which had reportedly caused civilian deaths and injuries.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Nigeria: 3 Killed in Attack On Hausa Quarters in Delta.
[Daily Trust] Three persons have been killed following an attack by suspected hoodlums on the Hausa quarters in Warri, Warri South Local Government Area of Delta State.

- Jerusalem Post, just now: US base in Bahrain remains low-staffed months after Iranian drone, missile strikes - report.
Despite negotiations between Washington and Tehran, Iranian attacks on Bahrain have not stopped, with the most recent attack targeting an undisclosed US military base in the country.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: IDF kills two Hamas terrorists who also worked for Doctors Without Borders, military says.
Doctors Without Borders condemns the IDF strike that killed Hamas terrorists working at an MSF clinic, calling for accountability, claiming it was a "direct attack on MSF."
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 2 hours ago: Iran war live: Italy says drone in deadly Kuwait attack was made in Iran.
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says the drone behind the deadly Kuwait strike was made in Iran.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Israel kills two MSF staff in targeted strike on Gaza clinic.
An Israeli strike on a clinic operated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Gaza has killed two watchmen.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: Malawian Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine War.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 20 hours ago: Malawi: Malawian Killed Fighting for Russia in Ukraine War.
[Nyasa Times] The family of a Malawian driver who vanished from Blantyre has been left reeling after learning he was killed while fighting for Russia against Ukraine.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Police to Name and Shame Companies Selling Counterfeit Agricultural Inputs.
[New Zimbabwe] THE Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) has warned that it will name and shame backyard garages, unregistered companies and individuals involved in manufacturing and selling counterfeit agricultural inputs to farmers.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 22 hours ago: South Africa: South Africa's Border Management Plans Drone Surveillance and Tighter Security for 2026/27 Festive Season.
[New Zimbabwe] The South African Border Management Authority (BMA) is preparing to intensify border security during the 2026/2027 festive season, including deploying drones at vulnerable crossing points to curb illegal activity.

Taiwan’s move to toughen up on exemptions to military service has sparked anxiety among some young men facing conscription and raised questions over whether expanding recruitment will actually strengthen the island’s combat readiness. While the government argues that limiting exemptions will make conscription fairer and ease personnel shortages, critics warn that recruiting men previously deemed medically unsuitable could endanger their health, complicate training and undermine morale. For five years, one name card has been missing from the grand circular table at the Association of Southeast Asean Nations biannual leaders’ summit: Min Aung Hlaing. As president of Myanmar, he should by diplomatic convention sit alongside the 10 other leaders of the Southeast Asian bloc at its regular get-togethers. China has for the first time sent its main battle tanks via an amphibious transport dock to Southeast Asia for a 15-day joint military exercise with Cambodia. The drills began on Wednesday at the Cambodia-China Joint Support and Training Centre, which opened early last year at Ream Port – a strategically located Cambodian naval base. - NK News, 20 hours ago: North Korean defector apprehended while moving toward inter-Korean border fence.
A North Korean defector moving north toward the inter-Korean border fence in Cheorwon County was apprehended by South Korean troops Thursday evening, according to Seoul’s defense authorities. India - bottom line: Rohtak hotel shooting: Killing was directed from Georgia, say sleuths.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Rohtak hotel shooting: Killing was directed from Georgia, say sleuths.
Authorities are investigating gangster Ravi Rathi's suspected role in a shocking quadruple murder tied to his rival, Sunny Ritoli. Operating from Georgia, Rathi's henchmen employed a honeytrap to bait Ritoli into a lethal ambush at a hotel, resulting in the deaths of three aides while Ritoli narrowly escaped. Investigative teams are intensifying efforts to pinpoint Rathi's whereabouts, bracing for any retaliation as tensions escalate following the attack on Ritoli's crew.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: OpenAI Accuses Apple Of Stealing Trade Secrets In New Lawsuit: Report.
OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, the Financial Times reported on Friday.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: MLA Awhad says NCP (SP) will back delimitation bill, Sule seeks draft first.
NCP (SP) MLA Jitendra Awhad confirmed the party's support for the delimitation bill after meeting Sharad Pawar. Baramati MP Supriya Sule stated that the party would examine the draft before making a decision. She will miss the INDIA bloc meeting due to her father's hospitalization, delegating the representation to Amol Kolhe. The Union cabinet has approved the proposed legislation, set for discussion during a special Lok Sabha session.

As many as 4,217 civil defence volunteers participated in the exercise, which covered several prominent locations, including the Dhaula Kuan Metro station, Kashmiri Gate ISBT and Gaffar Market in Karol Bagh.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Ukrainian psychiatrists training in Australia to treat trauma at home.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Ukrainian psychiatrists training in Australia to treat trauma at home.

- ABC News Australia, 3 hours ago: Unoccupied house collapses in Mornington Peninsula landslide.

- ABC News Australia, 5 hours ago: Hope for Christmas beetles after warm winter, wet spring.
Christmas beetles are a beloved Australian insect, one that can glow like a jewel and which heralds the arrival of the holiday season. But fears they are in decline have prompted calls for citizen scientists.
